```{r}
# function to reformat the lmer outcomes
coef.format <- function(object) {
  sc <- fixef(object)
  se <- coef(summary(object))[,"Std. Error"]
  result = data.frame(coef=sc, se=se)
  result$lower = result$coef-result$se*1.96
  result$upper = result$coef+result$se*1.96
  result$upper<-format(round(result$upper,2),nsmall=2)
  result$lower<-format(round(result$lower,2),nsmall=2)
  result$coef<-format(round(result$coef,2),nsmall=2)
  return(result)
}
```

```{r}
 data = read_excel('C:/users/hchen/Dropbox/PycharmProjects/false_mem/C. script_LMM/data_sheets/semantic_measures_0819b.xlsx',.name_repair = "universal" )

  group_by(story_id) %>%
  mutate(event_location = event_id / max(event_id)) %>%
  ungroup()
data$event_location = scale(data$event_location)
data$length = scale(data$length)
data$conflict = recode_data <- ifelse(is.na(data$conflict), NA, ifelse(data$conflict == 0, 1, ifelse(data$conflict == 1, 0, data$conflict)))

# data filled na with 0
data_fill =  replace(data, is.na(data), 0)
data_fill =  as.data.frame(data_fill)

# data with only the recalled trials
data_wrong=data[!is.na(data$false),]
```

# confict
```{r}
model_conflict = glmer(conflict ~ centrality+PPL_context+prior+length+event_location+(1|story_id)+(1|par_id), data = data_wrong,family = binomial(link = "logit"),control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa"))
summary(model_conflict)
anova(model_conflict)
vif(model_conflict)
coef.format(model_conflict)
```

# plot the separate models
```{r}
library(patchwork)

extract_coefs <- function(model) {
  s <- summary(model)
  coefs <- s$coefficients  # matrix of fixed-effect terms
  
  df <- data.frame(
    term     = rownames(coefs),
    Estimate = coefs[, "Estimate"],
    SE       = coefs[, "Std. Error"],
    pval     = coefs[, "Pr(>|z|)"]*4,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  # Exclude intercept if desired
  df <- df[df$term != "(Intercept)", ]
  df <- df[df$term != "length", ]

  # Significance stars
  df$stars <- ifelse(df$pval < 0.001, "***",
              ifelse(df$pval < 0.01,  "**",
              ifelse(df$pval < 0.05,  "*",
              ifelse(df$pval < 0.1,   ".", ""))))
  
  # Position to place star above/below the bar
  df$star_y <- ifelse(df$Estimate > 0,
                      df$Estimate + df$SE + 0.04,  # above for positive
                      df$Estimate - df$SE - 0.05)  # below for negative
  
  return(df)
}
make_bar_plot <- function(mod, model_title = "", remove_x = FALSE,
                          my_colors = NULL, bar_width = 0.7, ymax=0.38, show_legend = FALSE) {
  
  df <- extract_coefs(mod)
  
  # Reorder/rename your factors if desired
  df$term <- factor(df$term,
                    levels = c("centrality", "prior", "PPL_context","event_location","length"), 
  labels = c("semantic centrality", "sim. to prior corpus", "contextual surprisal","serial position","event length"))
  
  # Build the ggplot
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = term, y = Estimate, fill = term)) +
    # Bars
    geom_col(width = bar_width, show.legend = show_legend, alpha=0.7) +
    
    # Error bars (+/- 1 SE here, or use 1.96*SE for ~95% CI)
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Estimate - 1.96*SE, ymax = Estimate + 1.96*SE),
                  width = 0.1) +
    # Horizontal line
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
    
    # range of y
    ylim(-0.25, ymax) +

    # Significance stars
    geom_text(aes(label = stars, y = star_y),
              vjust = ifelse(df$Estimate > 0, 0, 1), # anchor above or below
              size = 5) +
    
    # Manual fill colors if provided
   (if (!is.null(my_colors)) scale_fill_manual(
  name = NULL,
  values = my_colors,
  guide = guide_legend(direction = "horizontal")) else NULL) +
    
    # Title and theme
    ggtitle(model_title) +
    theme_classic() +  # Start with theme_classic
    
    # Remove facet strips or boxes if you had used facet (not needed here).
    # But if you want no "box" behind the title, do:
    theme(
      # No box around the main title:
      plot.title = element_text(
        # face="bold", size=14, etc. if you want
        size = 10,
        margin = margin(b = 10)  # some spacing below the title
      ),
      # Control axis text font/size
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8),  # e.g. size=12
      axis.text.y = element_text(size=6.5),
      
      # Control axis title font/size
      axis.title.x = element_text(size=8),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size=8)
    ) +
    
    xlab("Predictors of interest") +
    ylab("Betas")
  
  # Optionally remove x-axis text/ticks/label if this is a "top" plot
  # and you only want x-axis on the bottom plot.
  if (remove_x) {
    p <- p + theme(
      axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
    )
  }
  
  return(p)
}

###############################################################################
# 5. Make four separate plots (one per model), stacking them with patchwork
###############################################################################
# You can define a consistent color scheme for the bars across models:
my_colors <- c("semantic centrality" = "#b179ea",  # example color
               "sim. to prior corpus" = "#56B4E9",
               "contextual surprisal" = "#009E73",
               "serial position" = "#555555",
               "event length" = "#999999")

bar_width = 0.6
# top plots: remove_x = TRUE so they have no x-axis
p1 <- make_bar_plot(model_recall, "Recall rate", remove_x = TRUE,  my_colors = my_colors, bar_width = bar_width)
#p2 <- make_bar_plot(model_false, "False memory rate", remove_x = TRUE,  my_colors = my_colors, bar_width = bar_width)
p3 <- make_bar_plot(model_conflict, "Factual error rate", remove_x = TRUE,  my_colors = my_colors, bar_width = bar_width)

# bottom plot: remove_x = FALSE so it shows x-axis
p4 <- make_bar_plot(model_confab, "Confabulation rate", remove_x = TRUE, my_colors = my_colors, bar_width = bar_width,show_legend=TRUE)

#p5 <- make_bar_plot(model_infer, "Inference rate", remove_x = FALSE, my_colors = my_colors, bar_width = bar_width, show_legend=TRUE)

# Combine them vertically with patchwork
p_combined <- p1 + p3 + p4 + plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

p_combined
```

###### multivariate model

```{r}
library(MCMCglmm)

# Suppose your data frame is called df_wide, with columns:
# df_wide$Y1, df_wide$Y2, df_wide$Y3, df_wide$Y4, A, B, C, Subject

# We want 4 Gaussian responses
n_outcomes <- 4

# Prior: we allow an unstructured (co)variance for both G (random) and R (residual) 
# Very loose/informative prior for illustration
prior_mv <- list(
  R = list(
    V = diag(n_outcomes),  # for 4 outcomes
    nu = 1
  ),
  G = list(
    G1 = list(V = diag(n_outcomes), nu = 2),  # matches us(trait):Subject
    G2 = list(V = diag(n_outcomes), nu = 2)   # matches us(trait):Item
  )
)

fixed_formula <- cbind(recall,false,confab,conflict) ~ trait - 1 + 
    trait:centrality+trait:PPL_context+trait:prior+trait:length+trait:event_location
random_formula <-  ~ us(trait):par_id + us(trait):story_id

# Model:
m_mv <- MCMCglmm(
  fixed = fixed_formula,  
  random = random_formula,  # unstructured covariance among the 4 traits by Subject
  rcov   = ~ idh(trait):units,    # unstructured residual covariance among the 4 traits
  family = rep("threshold", n_outcomes) ,
  data   = data_fill,
  prior  = prior_mv,
  nitt   = 30000,     # Increase for real data
  burnin = 5000,      # Increase for real data
  thin   = 10
)

summary(m_mv)

```
